1.en: MAN: Excuse me. Would you mind if I asked you some questions?
1.zh: 男士：不好意思。你介意我問你幾個問題嗎？

1.en: We’re doing a survey on transport.
1.zh: 我們正在做一項關於交通的調查。

1.en: SADIE: Yes, that’s OK.
1.zh: Sadie：可以，沒問題。

1.en: MAN: First of all, can I take your name?
1.zh: 男士：首先，可以請問你的姓名嗎？

1.en: SADIE: Yes. It’s Sadie Jones.
1.zh: Sadie：可以。我叫 Sadie Jones 。

1.en: MAN: Thanks very much.
1.zh: 男士：非常感謝。

1.en: And could I have your date of birth – just the year will do, actually.
1.zh: 可以請問你的出生日期嗎？ 其實只要年份就可以。

1.en: Is that all right?
1.zh: 這樣可以嗎？

1.en: SADIE: Yes, that’s fine. It’s 1991.
1.zh: Sadie：可以，沒問題。是 1991 年。

1.en: MAN: So next your postcode, please.
1.zh: 男士：接下來請告訴我你的郵遞區號。

1.en: SADIE: It’s DW30 7YZ.
1.zh: Sadie：是 DW30 7YZ。

1.en: MAN: Great. Thanks. Is that in Wells?
1.zh: 男士：太好了，謝謝。那是在 Wells 嗎？

1.en: SADIE: No, it’s actually in Harborne – Wells isn’t far from there, though.
1.zh: Sadie：不是，其實是在 Harborne，不過 Wells 離那裡不遠。

1.en: MAN: I really like that area.
1.zh: 男士：我很喜歡那一區。

1.en: My grandmother lived there when I was a kid.
1.zh: 我小時候，我祖母住在那裡。

1.en: SADIE: Yes, it is nice.
1.zh: Sadie：是啊，那裡很不錯。

1.en: MAN: Right, so now I want to ask you some questions about how you travelled here today.
1.zh: 男士：好的，現在我想問你一些關於今天怎麼來這裡的問題。

1.en: Did you use public transport?
1.zh: 你有使用公共交通嗎？

1.en: SADIE: Yes. I came by bus.
1.zh: Sadie：有。我是搭公車來的。

1.en: MAN: OK. And that was today.
1.zh: 男士：好的。那是今天。

1.en: It’s the 24th of April, isn’t it?
1.zh: 今天是 4 月 24 日，對吧？

1.en: SADIE: Isn’t it the 25th?
1.zh: Sadie：不是 25 日嗎？

1.en: No, actually, you’re right.
1.zh: 不，其實你是對的。

1.en: MAN: Ha ha. And what was the reason for your trip today?
1.zh: 男士：哈哈。那你今天出行的原因是什麼？

1.en: I can see you’ve got some shopping with you.
1.zh: 我看到你有買一些東西。

1.en: SADIE: Yes. I did some shopping but the main reason I came here was to go to the dentist.
1.zh: Sadie：是的。我買了些東西， 但我今天來這裡的主要原因是去看牙醫。

1.en: MAN: That’s not much fun.
1.zh: 男士：那可不太有趣。

1.en: Hope it was nothing serious.
1.zh: 希望不是什麼嚴重問題。

1.en: SADIE: No, it was just a check-up. It’s fine.
1.zh: Sadie：不是，只是例行檢查。 沒事。

1.en: MAN: Good. Do you normally travel by bus into the city centre?
1.zh: 男士：那就好。你平常也搭公車進市中心嗎？

1.en: SADIE: Yes. I stopped driving in ages ago because parking was so difficult to find and it costs so much.
1.zh: Sadie：是的。我很久以前就不開車進城了，因為停車位很難找，而且費用很高。

1.en: MAN: I see.
1.zh: 男士：我明白。

1.en: SADIE: The bus is much more convenient too.
1.zh: Sadie：公車也方便多了。

1.en: It only takes about 30 minutes.
1.zh: 只需要大約 30 分鐘。

1.en: MAN: That’s good. So where did you start your journey?
1.zh: 男士：那很好。那你今天是從哪裡開始搭車的？

1.en: SADIE: At the bus stop on Claxby Street.
1.zh: Sadie：在 Claxby Street 的公車站。

1.en: MAN: Is that C-L-A-X-B-Y?
1.zh: 男士：是 C-L-A-X-B-Y 嗎？

1.en: SADIE: That’s right.
1.zh: Sadie：沒錯。

1.en: MAN: And how satisfied with the service are you?
1.zh: 男士：那你對公車服務滿意嗎？

1.en: Do you have any complaints?
1.zh: 有什麼不滿嗎？

1.en: SADIE: Well, as I said, it’s very convenient and quick when it’s on time, but this morning it was late.
1.zh: Sadie：嗯，就像我說的，如果準時的話，它非常方便又快速，但今天早上它晚點了。

1.en: Only about 10 minutes, but still.
1.zh: 雖然只晚了大約 10 分鐘，但還是有點煩。

1.en: MAN: Yes, I understand that’s annoying.
1.zh: 男士：是的，我理解，那確實令人不快。

1.en: And what about the timetable?
1.zh: 那時刻表方面呢？

1.en: Do you have any comments about that?
1.zh: 你有什麼看法嗎？

1.en: SADIE: Mmm. I suppose I mainly use the bus during the day, but any time I’ve been in town in the evening – for dinner or at the cinema – I’ve noticed you have to wait a long time for a bus – there aren’t that many.
1.zh: Sadie：嗯。我主要是在白天搭公車，但只要晚上到城裡吃飯或看電影，我就發現要等很久才有公車，晚上班次不多。

1.en: MAN: OK, thanks. So now I’d like to ask you about your car use.
1.zh: 男士：好的，謝謝。那現在我想問你關於開車的情況。

1.en: SADIE: Well, I have got a car but I don’t use it that often.
1.zh: Sadie：嗯，我有車，但不常用。

1.en: Mainly just to go to the supermarket. But that’s about it really.
1.zh: 主要只是去超市時開，基本上就是這樣。

1.en: My husband uses it at the weekends to go to the golf club.
1.zh: 我丈夫週末會開它去高爾夫俱樂部。

1.en: MAN: And what about a bicycle?
1.zh: 男士：那自行車呢？

1.en: SADIE: I don’t actually have one at the moment.
1.zh: Sadie：我目前其實沒有自行車。

1.en: MAN: What about the city bikes you can rent?
1.zh: 男士：那可以租的城市自行車呢？

1.en: Do you ever use those?
1.zh: 你有用過嗎？

1.en: SADIE: No – I’m not keen on cycling there because of all the pollution.
1.zh: Sadie：沒有。我不太想在那裡騎車，因為污染太嚴重。

1.en: But I would like to get a bike – it would be good to use it to get to work.
1.zh: 不過我想買一輛自行車，用它上班應該不錯。

1.en: MAN: So why haven’t you got one now?
1.zh: 男士：那你為什麼現在還沒有呢？

1.en: SADIE: Well, I live in a flat – on the second floor and it doesn’t have any storage – so we’d have to leave it in the hall outside the flat.
1.zh: Sadie：嗯，我住在公寓二樓， 而且沒有儲藏空間，所以我們只能把自行車放在公寓外面的走廊。

1.en: MAN: I see. OK. Well, I think that’s all...
1.zh: 男士：我明白。好的，我想問題就到這裡……

2.en: Good evening, everyone. Let me start by welcoming you all to this talk and thanking you for taking the time to consider joining ACE voluntary organisation.
2.zh: 各位晚上好。首先歡迎大家來參加這場說明會，也感謝你們花時間考慮加入 ACE 志工組織。

2.en: ACE offers support to people and services in the local area and we’re now looking for more volunteers to help us do this.
2.zh: ACE 為當地居民和服務項目提供支援，我們現在正在尋找更多志工來協助這項工作。

2.en: By the way, I hope you’re all comfortable – we have brought in extra seats so that no one has to stand, but it does mean that the people at the back of the room may be a bit squashed.
2.zh: 順便說一下，希望大家都坐得舒服。我們加了額外座位，這樣就沒有人需要站著，但這也表示房間後面的人可能會有點擠。

2.en: We’ll only be here for about half an hour so, hopefully, that’s OK.
2.zh: 我們大概只會在這裡待半小時，所以希望這樣還可以。

2.en: One of the first questions we’re often asked is how old you need to be to volunteer.
2.zh: 我們經常被問到的第一個問題之一，就是志工需要幾歲。

2.en: Well, you can be as young as 16 or you can be 60 or over; it all depends on what type of voluntary work you want to do.
2.zh: 嗯，你可以年輕到 16 歲，也可以是 60 歲以上；這完全取決於你想做哪一類志工工作。

2.en: Other considerations, such as reliability, are crucial in voluntary work and age isn’t related to these, in our experience.
2.zh: 根據我們的經驗，其他因素，例如可靠性，在志工工作中非常重要，而年齡與這些因素並沒有直接關係。

2.en: Another question we get asked relates to training.
2.zh: 我們被問到的另一個問題和培訓有關。

2.en: Well, there’s plenty of that and it’s all face-to-face.
2.zh: 培訓很多，而且都是面對面進行。

2.en: What’s more, training doesn’t end when you start working for us – it takes place before, during and after periods of work.
2.zh: 更重要的是，培訓不會在你開始為我們工作後就結束；它會在工作前、工作期間和工作後持續進行。

2.en: Often, it’s run by other experienced volunteers as managers tend to prefer to get on with other things.
2.zh: 通常，培訓由其他有經驗的志工負責，因為經理通常更願意去處理其他事情。

2.en: Now, I would ask you to consider a couple of important issues before you decide to apply for voluntary work.
2.zh: 現在，在你決定申請志工工作之前，我想請你考慮幾個重要問題。

2.en: We don’t worry about why you want to be a volunteer – people have many different reasons that range from getting work experience to just doing something they’ve always wanted to do.
2.zh: 我們不會太在意你想成為志工的原因；人們有各種不同理由， 從想獲得工作經驗，到只是想做一直想做的事情都有。

2.en: But it is critical that you have enough hours in the day for whatever role we agree is suitable for you – if being a volunteer becomes stressful then it’s best not to do it at all.
2.zh: 但關鍵是，你每天必須有足夠時間投入我們認為適合你的角色；如果當志工變成壓力，那最好就不要做。

2.en: You may think that your income is important, but we don’t ask about that.
2.zh: 你可能認為收入很重要，但我們不會詢問這一點。

2.en: It’s up to you to decide if you can work without earning money.
2.zh: 是否能做無薪工作，由你自己決定。

2.en: What we value is dedication.
2.zh: 我們重視的是投入和奉獻。

2.en: Some of our most loyal volunteers earn very little themselves but still give their full energy to the work they do with us.
2.zh: 我們一些最忠誠的志工本身收入很少，但仍然全心投入與我們一起做的工作。

2.en: OK, so let’s take a look at some of the work areas that we need volunteers for and the sort of things that would help you in those.
2.zh: 好的，接下來我們看看一些需要志工的工作領域，以及哪些能力會對這些工作有幫助。

2.en: You may wish simply to help us raise money.
2.zh: 你可能只是想幫我們籌款。

2.en: If you have the creativity to come up with an imaginative or novel way of fundraising, we’d be delighted, as standing in the local streets or shops with a collection box can be rather boring!
2.zh: 如果你有創意，能想出有想像力或新穎的籌款方式，我們會非常高興，因為拿著募款箱站在當地街道或商店裡可能相當無聊！

2.en: One outdoor activity that we need volunteers for is litter collection and for this it’s useful if you can walk for long periods, sometimes uphill.
2.zh: 我們需要志工參與的一項戶外活動是撿拾垃圾；這項工作需要能長時間步行，有時還要走上坡。

2.en: Some of our regular collectors are quite elderly, but very active and keen to protect the environment.
2.zh: 我們一些固定參與撿垃圾的志工年紀較大，但非常活躍，也很熱心保護環境。

2.en: If you enjoy working with children, we have three vacancies for what are called “playmates”.
2.zh: 如果你喜歡和孩子一起工作， 我們有三個「玩伴」志工空缺。

2.en: These volunteers help children learn about staying healthy through a range of out-of-school activities.
2.zh: 這些志工會透過一系列課外活動，幫助孩子學習如何保持健康。

2.en: You don’t need to have children yourself, but it’s good if you know something about nutrition and can give clear instructions.
2.zh: 你自己不一定要有孩子，但如果你懂一些營養知識，並能清楚給出指示，那會很有幫助。

2.en: If that doesn’t appeal to you, maybe you would be interested in helping out at our story club for disabled children, especially if you have done some acting.
2.zh: 如果這不吸引你，也許你會對協助我們的身心障礙兒童故事俱樂部感興趣，尤其是如果你有表演經驗的話。

2.en: We put on three performances a year based on books they have read and we’re always looking for support with the theatrical side of this.
2.zh: 我們每年會根據孩子們讀過的書演出三場表演，因此一直在尋找能協助戲劇方面的人。

2.en: The last area I’ll mention today is first aid.
2.zh: 今天我要提到的最後一個領域是急救。

2.en: Volunteers who join this group can end up teaching others in vulnerable groups who may be at risk of injury.
2.zh: 加入這個小組的志工，最後可能會教導那些有受傷風險的弱勢群體。

2.en: Initially, though, your priority will be to take in a lot of information and not forget any important steps or details.
2.zh: 不過一開始，你的首要任務是吸收大量資訊，並且不要忘記任何重要步驟或細節。

2.en: Right, so does anyone have any questions…
2.zh: 好的，那麼有人有問題嗎……

3.en: HUGO: Hi Chantal. What did you think of the talk, then?
3.zh: Hugo：嗨，Chantal。你覺得這場講座怎麼樣？

3.en: CHANTAL: Hi Hugo. I thought it was good once I’d moved seats.
3.zh: Chantal：嗨，Hugo。我換了座位之後覺得還不錯。

3.en: HUGO: Oh – were the people beside you chatting or something?
3.zh: Hugo：哦——你旁邊的人在聊天之類的嗎？

3.en: CHANTAL: It wasn’t that.
3.zh: Chantal：不是那樣。

3.en: I went early so that I’d get a seat and not have to stand, but then this guy sat right in front of me and he was so tall!
3.zh: 我很早就去了，這樣就能有座位、不用站著，但後來有個人坐在我正前方，而且他非常高！

3.en: HUGO: It’s hard to see through people’s heads, isn’t it?
3.zh: Hugo：要透過別人的頭看東西很難，對吧？

3.en: CHANTAL: Impossible! Anyway, to answer your question, I thought it was really interesting, especially what the speaker said about the job market.
3.zh: Chantal：根本不可能！不過回答你的問題，我覺得講座真的很有趣，尤其是講者談到就業市場的部分。

3.en: HUGO: Me too. I mean we know we’re going into a really competitive field so it’s obvious that we may struggle to get work.
3.zh: Hugo：我也是。我的意思是，我們知道自己要進入一個競爭非常激烈的領域，所以很明顯我們可能會很難找到工作。

3.en: CHANTAL: That’s right – and we know we can’t all have that “dream job”.
3.zh: Chantal：沒錯，而且我們也知道，不可能每個人都得到那份「夢想工作」。

3.en: HUGO: Yeah, but it looks like there’s a whole range of areas of work that we hadn’t even thought of – like fashion journalism, for instance.
3.zh: Hugo：是啊，但看起來有一整個範圍的工作領域是我們根本沒想過的，例如時尚新聞。

3.en: CHANTAL: Yeah – I wasn’t expecting so many career options.
3.zh: Chantal：是啊，我沒想到有這麼多職業選擇。

3.en: HUGO: Mmm. Overall, she had quite a strong message, didn’t she?
3.zh: Hugo：嗯。整體來說，她傳達的訊息相當強烈，不是嗎？

3.en: CHANTAL: She did. She kept saying things like “I know you all think this, but…” and then she’d tell us how it really is.
3.zh: Chantal：是的。她一直說像是「我知道你們都這麼想，但是……」然後就告訴我們實際情況是怎樣。

3.en: HUGO: Perhaps she thinks students are a bit narrow-minded about the industry.
3.zh: Hugo：也許她覺得學生對這個行業的看法有點狹隘。

3.en: CHANTAL: It was a bit harsh, though!
3.zh: Chantal：不過她說得有點嚴厲！

3.en: We know it’s a tough industry.
3.zh: 我們知道這是一個很艱難的行業。

3.en: HUGO: Yeah – and we’re only first years, after all. We’ve got a lot to learn.
3.zh: Hugo：是啊，而且畢竟我們才一年級。我們還有很多要學。

3.en: CHANTAL: Exactly. Do you think our secondary-school education should have been more career-focused?
3.zh: Chantal：正是如此。你覺得我們的中學教育應該更重視職業規劃嗎？

3.en: HUGO: Well, we had numerous talks on careers, which was good, but none of them were very inspiring.
3.zh: Hugo：嗯，我們當時有很多職業講座，這點很好，但沒有一場特別鼓舞人心。

3.en: They could have asked more people like today’s speaker to talk to us.
3.zh: 他們本可以請更多像今天這位講者一樣的人來跟我們談。

3.en: CHANTAL: I agree. We were told about lots of different careers – just when we needed to be, but not by the experts who really know stuff.
3.zh: Chantal：我同意。我們確實在需要的時候聽到了很多不同職業的介紹，但不是由真正懂這個行業的專家來講。

3.en: HUGO: So did today’s talk influence your thoughts on what career you’d like to take up in the future?
3.zh: Hugo：那今天的講座有影響你對未來想從事哪種職業的想法嗎？

3.en: CHANTAL: Well, I promised myself that I’d go through this course and keep an open mind till the end.
3.zh: Chantal：嗯，我答應過自己會完成這門課程，並一直保持開放心態直到最後。

3.en: HUGO: But I think it’s better to pick an area of the industry now and then aim to get better and better at it.
3.zh: Hugo：但我覺得最好現在就選定這個行業中的某個領域，然後努力在那方面越做越好。

3.en: CHANTAL: Well, I think we’ll just have to differ on that issue!
3.zh: Chantal：嗯，我想在這件事上我們只能保留不同看法了！

3.en: HUGO: One thing’s for certain, though.
3.zh: Hugo：不過有一件事是肯定的。

3.en: From what she said, we’ll be unpaid assistants in the industry for quite a long time.
3.zh: 按她所說，我們會在這個行業裡做很長一段時間的無薪助理。

3.en: CHANTAL: Mmm.
3.zh: Chantal：嗯。

3.en: HUGO: I’m prepared for that, aren’t you?
3.zh: Hugo：我已經做好準備了，你呢？

3.en: CHANTAL: Actually, I’m not going to accept that view.
3.zh: Chantal：其實，我不打算接受那種看法。

3.en: HUGO: Really? But she knows it’s the case – and everyone else says the same.
3.zh: Hugo：真的嗎？但她知道情況就是這樣，而且其他人也都這麼說。

3.en: CHANTAL: That doesn’t mean it has to be true for me.
3.zh: Chantal：那不代表對我來說也一定會是這樣。

3.en: HUGO: OK. Well – I hope you’re right!
3.zh: Hugo：好吧。嗯——希望你是對的！

3.en: CHANTAL: I thought the speaker’s account of her first job was fascinating.
3.zh: Chantal：我覺得講者講她第一份工作的經歷很吸引人。

3.en: HUGO: Yeah – she admitted she was lucky to get work being a personal dresser for a musician.
3.zh: Hugo：是啊，她承認自己很幸運，能得到一份為音樂家做私人造型師的工作。

3.en: She didn’t even apply for the job and there she was getting paid to choose all his clothes.
3.zh: 她甚至沒有申請那份工作，就這樣得到了替他挑選所有服裝並拿薪水的機會。

3.en: CHANTAL: It must have felt amazing – though she said all she was looking for back then was experience, not financial reward.
3.zh: Chantal：那感覺一定很棒，雖然她說當時自己追求的是經驗，而不是金錢回報。

3.en: HUGO: Mmm. And then he was so mean, telling her she was more interested in her own appearance than his!
3.zh: Hugo：嗯。然後他很刻薄，說她比起他的外表，更關心自己的外表！

3.en: CHANTAL: But – she did realise he was right about that, which really made me think.
3.zh: Chantal：但她確實意識到他在這點上是對的，這真的讓我思考很多。

3.en: I’m always considering my own clothes but now I can see you should be focusing on your client!
3.zh: 我總是在考慮自己的衣服，但現在我明白應該把注意力放在客戶身上！

3.en: HUGO: She obviously regretted losing the job.
3.zh: Hugo：她顯然很後悔失去那份工作。

3.en: CHANTAL: Well, as she said, she should have hidden her negative feelings about him, but she didn’t.
3.zh: Chantal：嗯，正如她所說，她本應隱藏自己對他的負面感受，但她沒有。

3.en: HUGO: It was really brave the way she picked herself up and took that job in retail.
3.zh: Hugo：她重新振作並接受零售工作的做法真的很勇敢。

3.en: Fancy working in a shop after that!
3.zh: 在那之後居然去商店工作！

3.en: CHANTAL: Yeah – well, she recommended we all do it at some point.
3.zh: Chantal：是啊，不過她建議我們每個人在某個階段都應該去做做看。

3.en: I guess as a designer you’d get to find out some useful information, like how big or small the average shopper is.
3.zh: 我想作為設計師，你能獲得一些有用資訊，例如一般顧客的身形大小。

3.en: HUGO: I think that’s an issue for manufacturers, not designers.
3.zh: Hugo：我認為那是製造商要考慮的問題，不是設計師。

3.en: However, it would be useful to know if there’s a gap in the market – you know, an item that no one’s stocking but that consumers are looking for.
3.zh: 不過，如果知道市場上有缺口會很有用——也就是某種消費者正在找、但沒有人供貨的商品。

3.en: CHANTAL: Yeah, people don’t give up searching.
3.zh: Chantal：是啊，人們不會放棄尋找。

3.en: They also take things back to the store if they aren’t right.
3.zh: 如果東西不合適，他們也會退回商店。

3.en: HUGO: Yeah. Imagine you worked in an expensive shop and you found out the garments sold there were being returned because they fell apart in the wash!
3.zh: Hugo：是啊。想像一下，如果你在一家高級商店工作，卻發現那裡賣的衣服因為洗了就散掉而被退回！

3.en: CHANTAL: Yeah, it would be good to know that kind of thing.
3.zh: Chantal：是啊，知道那種事情會很有用。

3.en: HUGO: Yeah.
3.zh: Hugo：是啊。

4.en: For my presentation today I want to tell you about how groups of elephants have been moved and settled in new reserves.
4.zh: 在今天的簡報中，我想介紹大象群是如何被遷移並安置到新的保護區的。

4.en: This is known as translocation and has been carried out in Malawi in Africa in recent years.
4.zh: 這被稱為遷地轉移，近年來已在非洲的馬拉威進行。

4.en: The reason this is being done is because of overpopulation of elephants in some areas.
4.zh: 進行這項工作的原因，是某些地區的大象數量過多。

4.en: Overpopulation is a good problem to have and not one we tend to hear about very often.
4.zh: 數量過多算是一種好問題，而且也不是我們經常聽到的問題。

4.en: In Malawi’s Majete National Park the elephant population had been wiped out by poachers, who killed the elephants for their ivory.
4.zh: 在馬拉威的 Majete National Park，大象族群曾被偷獵者消滅，他們為了象牙而獵殺大象。

4.en: But in 2003, the park was restocked and effective law enforcement was introduced.
4.zh: 但在 2003 年，公園重新引入大象，並實施了有效的執法措施。

4.en: Since then, not a single elephant has been poached.
4.zh: 從那以後，沒有一頭大象遭到偷獵。

4.en: In this safe environment, the elephant population boomed.
4.zh: 在這個安全的環境中，大象數量迅速增加。

4.en: Breeding went so well that there were more elephants than the park could support.
4.zh: 繁殖非常成功，以至於大象數量超過了公園能承載的範圍。

4.en: This led to a number of problems.
4.zh: 這導致了一些問題。

4.en: Firstly, there was more competition for food, which meant that some elephants were suffering from hunger.
4.zh: 首先，食物競爭變得更加激烈， 這意味著有些大象正在挨餓。

4.en: As there was a limit to the amount of food in the national park, some elephants began looking further afield.
4.zh: 由於國家公園內的食物有限， 一些大象開始到更遠的地方尋找食物。

4.en: Elephants were routinely knocking down fences around the park, which then had to be repaired at a significant cost.
4.zh: 大象經常撞倒公園周圍的圍欄，而這些圍欄之後必須花費大量資金修復。

4.en: To solve this problem, the decision was made to move dozens of elephants from Majete National Park to Nkhotakota Wildlife Park, where there were no elephants.
4.zh: 為了解決這個問題，人們決定將數十頭大象從 Majete National Park 遷移到沒有大象的 Nkhotakota Wildlife Park。

4.en: But, obviously, attempting to move significant numbers of elephants to a new home 300 kilometres away is quite a challenge.
4.zh: 但顯然，試圖把大量大象遷移到 300 公里外的新家，是一項相當大的挑戰。

4.en: So how did this translocation process work in practice?
4.zh: 那麼，這個遷地轉移過程實際上是如何運作的呢？

4.en: Elephants were moved in groups of between eight and twenty, all belonging to one family.
4.zh: 大象以 8 到 20 頭為一組進行遷移，且每組都屬於同一個家族。

4.en: Because relationships are very important to elephants, they all had to be moved at the same time.
4.zh: 因為關係對大象非常重要，所以牠們必須同時被轉移。

4.en: A team of vets and park rangers flew over the park in helicopters and targeted a group, which were rounded up and directed to a designated open plain.
4.zh: 一隊獸醫和公園巡護員乘坐直升機飛越公園，鎖定一組大象， 然後將牠們圍起來，引導到指定的開闊平原。

4.en: The vets then used darts to immobilise the elephants – this was a tricky manoeuvre, as they not only had to select the right dose of tranquiliser for different-sized elephants but they had to dart the elephants as they were running around.
4.zh: 接著獸醫使用飛鏢讓大象失去行動能力——這是一項棘手的操作，因為他們不僅要根據大象不同體型選擇合適的鎮靜劑劑量，還必須在大象四處奔跑時射中牠們。

4.en: This also had to be done as quickly as possible so as to minimise the stress caused.
4.zh: 這也必須盡快完成，以盡量減少造成的壓力。

4.en: As soon as the elephants began to flop onto the ground, the team moved in to take care of them.
4.zh: 大象一開始倒在地上，團隊就立刻靠近照料牠們。

4.en: To avoid the risk of suffocation, the team had to make sure none of the elephants were lying on their chests because their lungs could be crushed in this position.
4.zh: 為避免窒息風險，團隊必須確保沒有任何大象趴在胸部上， 因為這種姿勢可能會壓傷牠們的肺。

4.en: So all the elephants had to be placed on their sides.
4.zh: 因此所有大象都必須側躺。

4.en: One person stayed with each elephant while they waited for the vets to do checks.
4.zh: 在等待獸醫檢查時，每頭大象旁邊都有一個人陪著。

4.en: It was very important to keep an eye on their breathing – if there were fewer than six breaths per minute, the elephant would need urgent medical attention.
4.zh: 密切觀察牠們的呼吸非常重要 ——如果每分鐘少於六次呼吸，大象就需要緊急醫療處理。

4.en: Collars were fitted to the matriarch in each group so their movements could be tracked in their new home.
4.zh: 每組中的母象首領都被戴上項圈，這樣就可以追蹤牠們在新棲地中的活動。

4.en: Measurements were taken of each elephant’s tusks – elephants with large tusks would be at greater risk from poachers – and also of their feet.
4.zh: 工作人員測量了每頭大象的象牙，因為象牙較大的大象更容易遭到偷獵；同時也測量了牠們的腳。

4.en: The elephants were then taken to a recovery area before being loaded onto trucks and transported to their new home.
4.zh: 隨後，大象被帶到恢復區，然後裝上卡車，運往牠們的新家。

4.en: The elephants translocated to Nkhotakota settled in very well and the project has generally been accepted to have been a huge success – and not just for the elephants.
4.zh: 被遷移到 Nkhotakota 的大象適應得很好，而這個項目普遍被認為非常成功——而且不只是對大象而言。

4.en: Employment prospects have improved enormously, contributing to rising living standards for the whole community.
4.zh: 就業機會大幅改善，促進了整個社區生活水準的提高。

4.en: Poaching is no longer an issue, as former poachers are able to find more reliable sources of income.
4.zh: 偷獵不再是問題，因為過去的偷獵者現在能找到更可靠的收入來源。

4.en: In fact, many of them volunteered to give up their weapons, as they were no longer of any use to them.
4.zh: 事實上，他們當中許多人主動交出武器，因為那些武器對他們來說已經沒有用處。

4.en: More than two dozen elephants have been born at Nkhotakota since relocation.
4.zh: 自遷移以來，Nkhotakota 已有二十多頭大象出生。

4.en: With an area of more than 1,800 square kilometres, there’s plenty of space for the elephant population to continue to grow.
4.zh: 由於面積超過 1,800 平方公里， 這裡有足夠空間讓大象族群繼續增長。

4.en: Their presence is also helping to rebalance Nkhotakota’s damaged ecosystem and providing a sustainable conservation model, which could be replicated in other parks.
4.zh: 牠們的存在也有助於重新平衡 Nkhotakota 受損的生態系統， 並提供一種可持續的保育模式，可供其他公園借鑑。

4.en: All this has been a big draw for tourism, which contributes five times more than the illegal wildlife trade to GDP, and this is mainly because of the elephants.
4.zh: 這一切對旅遊業產生了巨大吸引力，而旅遊業對 GDP 的貢獻是非法野生動物貿易的五倍， 這主要是因為大象。

4.en: There’s also been a dramatic rise in interest...
4.zh: 人們對此的興趣也大幅增加……

1.explanation: 題目寫： “Postcode: _____” 錄音直接問： “So next your postcode, please.” Sadie 回答： “It’s DW30 7YZ.” 所以答案是 DW30 7YZ。 這類 postcode 題最重要的是準確抄寫英文字母與數字。後面提到 Harborne 和 Wells，都是地點名稱，與郵遞區號本身無關。

2.explanation: 題目寫： “Date of bus journey: _____” 錄音中男士先確認： “It’s the 24th of April, isn’t it?” Sadie 一度以為是 25 日： “Isn’t it the 25th?” 但她立即修正： “No, actually, you’re right.” 所以最終確認的日期是 24 April / April 24th。 中伏位：25th 是 Sadie 一瞬間的誤記，隨後被她自己推翻。IELTS 日期題很常出現「先提出另一個日期，再確認正確日期」的安排，因此要聽最後確認。

3.explanation: 題目寫： “Reason for trip: shopping and visit to the _____” 錄音說： “I did some shopping but the main reason I came here was to go to the dentist.” 題目已經把 shopping 寫出來，所以另一個目的就是去看 dentist。 答案是 dentist。 後面提到 “just a check-up”，只是說明看牙醫的原因和嚴重程度，空格仍然問去哪裡。

4.explanation: 題目寫： “Travelled by bus because cost of _____ too high” Sadie 解釋自己很久以前已經不開車進市中心： “because parking was so difficult to find and it costs so much.” 這裡有兩個問題： ● parking spaces 難找 ● parking 費用很高題目抽取第二點，所以： cost of parking too high 答案是 parking。

5.explanation: 題目寫： “Got on bus at _____ Street” 錄音說： “At the bus stop on Claxby Street.” 男士還特別確認拼字： “Is that C-L-A-X-B-Y?” Sadie 回答： “That’s right.” 所以空格只填 Claxby。 題目已經有 Street，不需要重複寫整個街名。

6.explanation: 題目寫： “Complaints about bus service: bus today was _____” Sadie 說： “it’s very convenient and quick when it’s on time, but this morning it was late.” 所以今天的投訴是巴士 late。 後面 “about 10 minutes” 只是說明晚點多久；題目空格需要描述巴士狀態的形容詞。

7.explanation: 題目寫： “frequency of buses in the _____” Sadie 說自己白天主要乘巴士，但： “any time I’ve been in town in the evening … you have to wait a long time for a bus – there aren’t that many.” “there aren’t that many” 指班次較少，因此題目的 complaint 是 evening bus frequency。 答案是 evening。 中伏位：day 也有出現，但她沒有抱怨白天班次；問題集中在晚上。

8.explanation: 題目寫： “Goes to the _____ by car” Sadie 說自己雖然有車，但： “Mainly just to go to the supermarket.” 所以她主要開車去 supermarket。 中伏位：她丈夫會開車去 golf club，但題目問的是 Sadie 自己的 car use。

9.explanation: 題目寫： “Dislikes travelling by bike in the city centre because of the _____” Sadie 談到租用 city bikes 時說： “I’m not keen on cycling there because of all the pollution.” 所以答案是 pollution。 這裡 “there” 指 city centre，因此題目完整改寫為：她不喜歡在市中心騎車，原因是污染。

10.explanation: 題目寫： “Doesn’t own a bike because of a lack of _____” Sadie 說自己住在二樓 flat： “it doesn’t have any storage – so we’d have to leave it in the hall outside the flat.” 沒有地方安全存放自行車，因此她目前沒有買 bike。 所以答案是 storage。 這一題的邏輯是： flat has no storage → bike would have to stay outside → she has not bought one

11.answer: C — Some of them are very close together
11.explanation: 題目問：speaker 為甚麼就座位安排道歉。 錄音說他們額外搬入 seats，確保沒有人需要站著： “we have brought in extra seats so that no one has to stand” 但結果是： “the people at the back of the room may be a bit squashed.” “a bit squashed” 表示後排座位之間非常擠，與 some seats are very close together 最接近。 所以答案是 C。 中伏位：座位數目其實足夠，所以 B 不合；錄音也沒有說 seats 本身尺寸太小。

12.answer: A — The age of volunteers is less important than other factors
12.explanation: 題目問 speaker 對志工年齡有甚麼看法。 錄音先說： “you can be as young as 16 or you can be 60 or over” 接著指出真正重要的因素： “Other considerations, such as reliability, are crucial … and age isn’t related to these.” 所以 speaker 的重點是：年齡範圍很廣，可靠性等個人特質更重要。 因此答案是 A。 B 沒有得到支持；speaker 沒有說年輕志工較不可靠。C 也只是把錄音中的 “60 or over” 誤當作大部分人的實際年齡。

13.explanation: 題目問 ACE 的 training 有甚麼特點。 錄音說： “training doesn’t end when you start working for us” 更具體地： “it takes place before, during and after periods of work.” 工作前、工作中、工作後都有培訓，表示 training 是持續進行的。 所以答案是 A — It is continuous。 中伏位：training 是 face-to-face，所以 C 不合；通常由 experienced volunteers 負責，也沒有以 manager 為主要 trainer。

14.explanation: 題目問：申請 volunteer 前，speaker 要大家特別考慮哪兩個問題。 B — their level of commitment 錄音說： “What we value is dedication.” 又形容優秀志工會： “give their full energy to the work” dedication 就是投入程度、承諾程度，因此對應 level of commitment。 所以 B 正確。 E — their availability speaker 說： “it is critical that you have enough hours in the day for whatever role…” 如果 voluntary work 令生活變得過度有壓力，便不適合參加。 “have enough hours” 直接涉及是否有足夠時間可供志工工作，所以對應 availability。 因此 E 正確。 中伏位：income 有被提到，但 ACE “don’t ask about that”；work experience 和個人 ambition 只是人們成為志工的可能原因，組織沒有把它們列為申請前最重要的考量。

15.explanation: 題目問：申請 volunteer 前，speaker 要大家特別考慮哪兩個問題。 B — their level of commitment 錄音說： “What we value is dedication.” 又形容優秀志工會： “give their full energy to the work” dedication 就是投入程度、承諾程度，因此對應 level of commitment。 所以 B 正確。 E — their availability speaker 說： “it is critical that you have enough hours in the day for whatever role…” 如果 voluntary work 令生活變得過度有壓力，便不適合參加。 “have enough hours” 直接涉及是否有足夠時間可供志工工作，所以對應 availability。 因此 E 正確。 中伏位：income 有被提到，但 ACE “don’t ask about that”；work experience 和個人 ambition 只是人們成為志工的可能原因，組織沒有把它們列為申請前最重要的考量。

16.explanation: 題目活動是 Fundraising。 錄音說： “If you have the creativity to come up with an imaginative or novel way of fundraising, we’d be delighted.” imaginative / novel = 有創意、具新意。 所以 fundraising 最有幫助的是： B — original, new ideas

17.answer: G — a good level of fitness
17.explanation: 題目活動是 Litter collection。 錄音說： “it’s useful if you can walk for long periods, sometimes uphill.” 長時間步行甚至上坡，需要良好的體能。 所以答案是 G — a good level of fitness。 錄音也說一些 elderly volunteers 仍然 “very active”，進一步說明年齡並非關鍵，體能才是工作所需。

18.answer: D — an understanding of food and diet
18.explanation: 題目活動是 “Playmates”。 這些 volunteers 幫助孩子學習： “staying healthy” speaker 接著說： “it’s good if you know something about nutrition” nutrition 就是食物、飲食與健康方面的知識，因此答案是： D — an understanding of food and diet 中伏位：你不需要自己有小孩，所以 C parenting skills 沒有被列為必要優勢。

19.explanation: 題目活動是 Story club。 錄音說： “especially if you have done some acting.” 原因是 story club 每年會： “put on three performances” 而且需要協助： “the theatrical side of this.” acting + performances + theatrical 都直接指向舞台經驗。 所以答案是 A。

20.explanation: 題目活動是 First aid。 錄音說初期 volunteer 的重點是： “take in a lot of information and not forget any important steps or details.” 如果要記住大量資訊、步驟和細節，良好記憶力會很有幫助。 所以答案是 F — a good memory。

21.answer: A — Her view of the speaker was blocked
21.explanation: 題目問 Chantal 在 talk 一開始遇到甚麼問題。 她說自己早到，也確實找到 seat，但： “this guy sat right in front of me and he was so tall!” Hugo 回： “It’s hard to see through people’s heads” Chantal 更說： “Impossible!” 所以問題是前面的人太高，擋住她看 speaker 的視線。 答案是 A。

22.answer: B — There is more variety in it than they had realised
22.explanation: 題目問 Hugo 和 Chantal 對 fashion job market 的哪一點感到驚訝。 Hugo 說： “there’s a whole range of areas of work that we hadn’t even thought of” 例如 fashion journalism。 Chantal 同意： “I wasn’t expecting so many career options.” 所以驚訝之處是職業選擇比他們原先想像多。 答案是 B。 中伏位：他們早已知道 fashion industry competitive，所以 A 並沒有令他們感到意外。

23.answer: A — unfair to them at times
23.explanation: 題目問兩人如何看 speaker 的 message。 Chantal 說 speaker 經常先指出學生的想法，再直接糾正： “She kept saying things like ‘I know you all think this, but…’” Hugo 覺得 speaker 可能認為學生： “a bit narrow-minded” Chantal 評價： “It was a bit harsh” Hugo 又指出： “we’re only first years, after all. We’ve got a lot to learn.” 所以兩人覺得 speaker 某些說法對他們這些一年級學生過於嚴厲，與 unfair to them at times 最接近答案是 A。

24.explanation: 題目問兩人批評中學 career advice 的哪一方面。 Hugo 說他們以前： “had numerous talks on careers” 所以 advice 數量其實不少。 Chantal 又說： “just when we needed to be” 所以 timing 也沒有問題。 真正問題是： “not by the experts who really know stuff.” 因此他們批評的是提供 advice 的人缺少真正行業專業。 答案是 C — who gave the advice。

25.answer: B — when to choose a career in fashion
25.explanation: Chantal 說自己打算： “keep an open mind till the end.” 她不想現在就鎖定一個 fashion career。 Hugo 的態度相反： “it’s better to pick an area of the industry now” Chantal 回： “we’ll just have to differ on that issue!” 所以分歧點是何時應選定職業方向。答案是 B。

26.answer: A — He is realistic about the practice
26.explanation: 題目問 Hugo 對做 unpaid assistant 有甚麼態度。 他說： “we’ll be unpaid assistants in the industry for quite a long time.” 接著： “I’m prepared for that” Chantal 不願接受這種情況，但 Hugo 認為 speaker 和其他人都說這是業界現實。 因此 Hugo 的態度比較務實：知道這種做法存在，也已做好心理準備。 所以答案是 A — realistic about the practice。

27.explanation: 題目問 speaker 承認自己第一份工作犯過哪兩個錯誤。 B — paying too much attention to how she looked 她的 client 批評她： “she was more interested in her own appearance than his” Chantal 補充 speaker 後來： “did realise he was right about that” 所以 speaker 承認自己太關心個人形象，沒有把 client 放在首位。 因此 B 正確。 E — openly disliking her client Chantal 說： “she should have hidden her negative feelings about him, but she didn’t.” 即使她不喜歡這位 client，工作上也應控制和隱藏這種負面態度。 她承認自己沒有做到，所以 E 正確。 中伏位：她當時想取得的是 experience，沒有追求大量收入，所以 D 沒有支持。

28.explanation: 題目問 speaker 承認自己第一份工作犯過哪兩個錯誤。 B — paying too much attention to how she looked 她的 client 批評她： “she was more interested in her own appearance than his” Chantal 補充 speaker 後來： “did realise he was right about that” 所以 speaker 承認自己太關心個人形象，沒有把 client 放在首位。 因此 B 正確。 E — openly disliking her client Chantal 說： “she should have hidden her negative feelings about him, but she didn’t.” 即使她不喜歡這位 client，工作上也應控制和隱藏這種負面態度。 她承認自己沒有做到，所以 E 正確。 中伏位：她當時想取得的是 experience，沒有追求大量收入，所以 D 沒有支持。

29.explanation: 題目問 Hugo 和 Chantal 都認為哪些 retail information 對 fashion designer 有用。 A — the reasons people return fashion items Chantal 提到顧客會把不合適商品退回商店。 Hugo 舉例： “garments … were being returned because they fell apart in the wash!” Chantal 回： “it would be good to know that kind of thing.” 所以了解顧客退貨的原因，對設計師有直接價值。 因此 A 正確。 C — fashion designs people want but can’t find Hugo 說： “it would be useful to know if there’s a gap in the market” 並解釋： “an item that no one’s stocking but that consumers are looking for.” 這就是消費者想買、但目前市場找不到的設計。 Chantal 也同意： “people don’t give up searching.” 所以 C 正確。 中伏位：Chantal 曾提平均顧客身形，但 Hugo 認為這較屬於 manufacturers 的問題，所以 E 沒有得到兩人共同支持。

31.explanation: 題目寫： “damage to _____ in the park” 錄音說 elephant population 過多後，一些大象為尋找更多食物走得更遠： “Elephants were routinely knocking down fences around the park” 而且維修： “at a significant cost.” 所以 overpopulation 導致的另一個問題就是破壞 fences。 答案是 fences。 這裡的因果關係是： 食物不足 → 大象往更遠處覓食 → 撞倒公園圍欄 → 產生高昂維修成本

32.explanation: 題目寫： “a suitable group of elephants from the same _____ was selected” 錄音說： “Elephants were moved in groups of between eight and twenty, all belonging to one family.” 之所以要維持同一家族： “relationships are very important to elephants” 所以遷移單位必須保留原有 family group。 答案是 family。

33.explanation: 題目寫： “vets and park staff made use of _____ to help guide the elephants into an open plain” 錄音說： “A team of vets and park rangers flew over the park in helicopters” 然後： “rounded up and directed [the elephants] to a designated open plain.” 所以 helicopters 讓工作人員從空中鎖定大象群，並協助把牠們趕往指定平原。 答案是 helicopters。

34.explanation: 題目寫： “this process had to be completed quickly to reduce _____” 錄音談到使用 tranquiliser darts 時說： “This also had to be done as quickly as possible so as to minimise the stress caused.” minimise = reduce，因此答案是 stress。 這裡的重點是 immobilisation 本身會令大象承受壓力，所以整個射鎮靜劑的過程需要快速完成。

35.explanation: 題目寫： “elephants had to be turned on their _____ to avoid damage to their lungs” 錄音解釋大象倒下後的風險： “none of the elephants were lying on their chests because their lungs could be crushed” 所以工作人員需要： “all the elephants had to be placed on their sides.” 完整因果是： 趴在胸口 → 身體重量可能壓迫肺部 → 有 suffocation 風險 → 必須側躺因此答案是 sides。

36.explanation: 題目寫： “elephants’ _____ had to be monitored constantly” 錄音說： “It was very important to keep an eye on their breathing” 而且提供具體安全指標： “if there were fewer than six breaths per minute, the elephant would need urgent medical attention.” 所以 monitoring 的對象是大象的 breathing。 答案是 breathing。 這不只是一般觀察；呼吸頻率直接用來判斷鎮靜後的大象是否出現危險。

37.explanation: 題目寫： “data including the size of their tusks and _____ was taken” 錄音說： “Measurements were taken of each elephant’s tusks … and also of their feet.” 所以除了 tusks，工作人員也測量 feet。 答案是 feet。 中伏位：collars 也在同一段出現，但 collars 是用來追蹤 matriarchs，並非測量資料的一部分。

38.explanation: 題目在 Nkhotakota translocation 的 advantages 下寫： “_____ opportunities” 錄音說： “Employment prospects have improved enormously, contributing to rising living standards for the whole community.” employment prospects improved = employment opportunities increased。 所以答案是 employment。 這項好處不只影響個別工作者，也提高整個 community 的 living standards，因此屬於 translocation 帶來的社會經濟效益。

39.explanation: 題目寫： “a reduction in the number of poachers and _____” 錄音先說： “Poaching is no longer an issue” 原因是 former poachers 現在有： “more reliable sources of income.” 接著說： “many of them volunteered to give up their weapons, as they were no longer of any use to them.” 所以 translocation 帶來新的就業與收入來源後，部分過去的 poachers 不再需要靠偷獵維生，並主動交出 weapons。 這裡可以看到完整因果鏈： 更多正規收入 → 偷獵下降 → former poachers 放棄武器 → poachers 和 weapons 數量都減少所以答案是 weapons。

40.explanation: 題目寫： “an increase in _____ as a contributor to GDP” 錄音說這個 conservation success： “has been a big draw for tourism” 並進一步指出 tourism： “contributes five times more than the illegal wildlife trade to GDP” 所以大象成功遷移、野生動物恢復，加強了 Nkhotakota 對遊客的吸引力；遊客增加後，tourism 對當地經濟與 GDP 的貢獻亦上升。 因此答案是 tourism。 這一題的邏輯可以整理成： elephant population restored → park 更具吸引力 → tourism 增長 → tourism 對 GDP 的貢獻提高題目把錄音中的 “big draw for tourism” 和 “contributes … to GDP” 合併成 an increase in tourism as a contributor to GDP。
